newsitem.title: FRANCE: No disaster if Poland in EU after 2000 - Kwasniewski.
newsitem.headline: No disaster if Poland in EU after 2000 - Kwasniewski.

text.p: Polish President Alexander Kwasniewski said in an interview published on Monday that he wanted Poland to join the European Union by the year 2000 but it would not be a disaster if the date slipped to 2001.

French President Jacques Chirac said on a visit to Warsaw in September that he hoped Poland could join by the year 2000. But the European Commission, the EU's executive, said Polish accession could realistically be envisaged only by 2002.
"So much the better if it is the year 2000," Kwasniewski told the daily Liberation. "But it won't be a disaster if it's 2001."

He added: "If President Chirac and (German) Chancellor (Helmut) Kohl talk about the year 2000, as the President of Poland I'm not going to disagree... It's important for our public opinion, it gives a near-term target.
"But, if one is realistic, the most important thing is to start negotiations -- and I hope that those will begin on January 1, 1998 -- and to be well prepared. And that's what we're doing."

Kwasniewski also said the United States, Europe and Russia should seize what he called "an exceptional five minutes in history" after the end of the Cold War to build a world without power blocs through an expanded NATO.
Asked if his reference to just five minutes meant he feared a more aggressive Russia, he replied: "Such a scenario is obviously possible."
He added: "Russian politicians have a responsibility to explain that NATO enlargement is not directed against Russia. The problem is that they use it in their internal political arguments."
